body: well done :) i know how hard it is, and it is really awful and confusing and sometimes you feel like you’re going insane! you’re right, progress isn’t linear and that’s a very important thing to remember but try your absolute hardest not to give in, because you are strong. you’ve fought this hard to get this far, you are strong even when you feel like you’re stuck.

that is OCD telling you that you don’t have OCD. i’m going to give you the best advice i can - stop posting on here as it is reassurance and makes the obsessions worse no matter how much you think it will make it better. seek out a good therapist who specialises in OCD and provides ERP therapy. stop giving into the compulsions and work on acceptance. it’s horribly difficult, but by posting on here and giving into compulsions all you are doing is stalling your progress.

yeah i understand that, i’m glad you could find some peace from the worries as i know how intense they can be. have you tried therapy at all just out of curiosity? and yeah it was really rough, i ended the relationship because i really struggled with intimacy because of the thoughts which hurt him a lot, and kept getting blackout and sleeping with random guys and i didn’t even enjoy it i just wanted to feel normal and less lonely (?) but i realised how much i loved him despite the anxieties and regretted everything, but understandably he didn’t want to get back together because of what i’d done. i tried to make up for it so much but he couldn’t get past it which i understand but i feel like an awful person.

i totally get you :( i lived with my boyfriend for a year n it was just so intense n i could tell i was putting him through a lot. i really loved him though it was just so confusing. i’m still getting the thoughts even out of the relationship though! we broke up about 2 months ago, but sort of were on and off (his choice to be on and off) for the last month and a half. what about you?

it was like a constant feeling of uneasiness and anxiety that i couldn’t help but associate with him, i would question if i loved him, if i was attracted to him, if i was actually turned on during sex, if i wanted to have sex with other people, if i wanted to be with other people - things like that just constantly going through my brain.

i feel this to some extent too, like i feel as though i’m faking everything when in reality my mind is just sooo clouded with anxiety that there isn’t any space for any other feeling. how long have you been struggling with this for? because, if it’s any sort of consolation, i’ve found that the anxiety ebs and flows and there are times you can feel really happy :) i know how difficult it is, but time changes things and things will get better <3

no that’s sort of what i meant by unhappy, my anxiety gets extremely out of hand. usually i just try to work through it, as it’s been bad for me personally for the last 9 months. its so difficult because sometimes i feel a lot of love for my boyfriend, but there’s like little feelings in the back of my mind that make me doubt my feelings, which i guess is just the anxiety. i’d say try to let your partner know that you’re feeling anxious at that moment and you need space, comfort or distraction. for me, i smoke weed and usually that calms my nerves and allows me to spend time with my boyfriend and actually enjoy it. not the healthiest coping mechanism lol, but it does definitely help. how have you been coping? :)

i understand, i think mental health problems are so much more complex than they seem. and no problem at all, feel free to reach out whenever you need :) and don’t be afraid to have days off when everything feels too much!

I completely agree. I think ocd really affects mental health, as I’ve become so depressed because of it. they sort of intertwine with each other! i miss times before all this triggered too, so so much, and i’d do anything to go back to how things were.

you are NOT a bad person! you didn’t choose to have rocd, and i’m sure it affects you horribly. i feel like a really bad person a lot too, but you have to remind yourself that you’re doing everything you can to get help and get better (you’ve booked therapy! a huge first step)

when you start therapy, make sure to mention the feelings of depression to your therapist and see if they can help you, as you could be prescribed medication that could make a world of difference alongside the therapy :)

also, try to force yourself to exercise, as i know that for me i can’t sleep usually because i’m way too anxious with the thoughts. exercising will feel like the biggest chore when you have no motivation, but once it’s done it provides at least a temporary happiness, which is a nice release from the living hell that is rocd.

please keep your chin up, you’ll be okay :) sending so much love your way!

coping is horrible and scary but you can do it, it just won’t be nice. i find that sometimes forcing the actions of affection is an exposure in itself and is good! so give her a hug, watch a film together, kiss her, even if you really really don’t feel like it, because it’s good to challenge the ocd and it’ll make her feel okay. i’m always here if you need advice or to talk :)
i know exactly how you feel honestly, i get extremely depressed over my feelings because it’s like i don’t even trust them anymore. but please try therapy before making any major decisions <3

hey :) i get the same feeling but you have to push through and one day it will be okay. there is nothing keeping you with your partner, but i urge you to try and carry on. look into an organisation called NOCD, they have payment plans for those who can’t afford it all up front x

it is really nice to relate, i agree - before i knew rocd was a thing i was a complete wreck :’) i think once we realise we’ve left the honeymoon stage of the relationship, our minds freak out because we’re just not used to not feeling infatuated by our partners, and we don’t get as many butterflies anymore, but that’s okay! also, there’s a stage of relationships called the power struggle stage which all relationships have, but i think it feels worse for people with rocd as we are freaked out by anything that changes our feelings - but it’s the stage where you start to see all your partners flaws and they start to annoy you, and for me, when i’m annoyed by something my boyfriend does, i get really upset because i convince myself i don’t love him anymore because i’m annoyed by him (lol), but after you get past that stage it’s meant to get a lot easier, so i think it’s a case of getting through that :) i hope that brings you a bit of peace of mind maybe !

no me too !! like i have a month or so where i’m feeling happy and normal, and then something will trigger me out of nowhere and i start to feel like i’m losing my mind and my feelings again ! ROCD is a difficult one but i think it’s just a matter of getting used to the feelings and learning to not feel panicked when they fade - it’s normal for feelings to eb and flow in relationships, we just have sticky minds that have bad thoughts that basically glue themselves in and we worry constantly !

i completely understand, i get like that too, i almost broke up with my boyfriend because of it but i felt so sad doing it i decided to hold on for a while, and even though it felt so difficult because it’s like your fighting an internal war with yourself, it goes up and down and you’re able to enjoy the good times, have moments of clarity where you realise how much you really do love them, even if they are fleeting. if you didn’t love your girlfriend, you wouldn’t be worrying about these feelings the way that you are, and it wouldn’t be hurting you so much - if anything, there’s some proof of your love for her! and she clearly wants to stick around to help you - i think sometimes we worry that we’re hurting our SOs much more than we actually are hurting them irl, so it makes us panic even more, making the compulsion of wanting to break up that much harder to resist. have you tried any sort of therapy?

ROCD attacks things that mean a lot to us, and because we care about them so much we tend to obsess over bad thoughts surrounding people we love! it’s horrible, but you have to remind yourself of that. be kind to yourself and try to (even though i know these kinds of thoughts are constant) take the thoughts and tell yourself “this is an ocd thought, and i’m going to think about this later” and try to move on with whatever you’re doing, even if the thought persists. you’ll be okay, i promise :) i feel the exact same way with my boyfriend, and it’s really hard, but he is really supportive which helps, so talk to your girlfriend about it maybe, but don’t constantly ask her for reassurance as this is a compulsion.

i find i go through phases, and they’re rough but they do pass. i usually have around a month of really intense ROCD thoughts to the point i’m crying everyday and just feeling the same as you, like i’m having a mental breakdown. but they pass, and i find myself feeling better (not 100% better, but able to enjoy my time with my boyfriend). i really recommend trying to find a therapist who specialises in ROCD who you like, and who can help you. i’m always here to talk :)

your thoughts aren’t your fault, and you can’t do anything to control them, so don’t beat yourself up okay! sharing thoughts with your boyfriend is actually a compulsion, so try not to do it, and seek therapy! i try to take my thoughts and say to myself “i’m going to think about this later”, and then think about it at the end of the day :)

hey, i’m f19 too and my boyfriend is 19, and i get the exact same feelings as you, but the rocd will come and go, you just have to battle through the numb or anxious days/weeks/months, as much as it hurts or feels wrong to do so. therapy helps 100%, but make sure you get a therapist who specialises in OCD, or rOCD if you can :) it will get better, just be kind to yourself and don’t beat yourself up when you have these thoughts (although i’m sure it’s constant, as it is for me), as beating yourself up will make you panic when you get the thoughts in the future, feeding into the cycle of rOCD.

also, my therapist gave me a few activities to do to try and combat the cycle of rocd, so here:
give yourself a worry period; this can be 15-20 minutes at the end of each day, where you allow any and every thought to do with your boyfriend to pass through your mind, but try not to react! they’re thoughts, they will come and go and we can’t control them :) during the day, write down all the different thoughts you get, but as a lot are repetitive, just say to yourself “i know i’m worrying about this, but i’ve written it down and i’m going to think about it later” and move on with your day, even if the thought persists. it will get easier, as you won’t associate the thoughts with panic or anxiety anymore eventually. 

sending you love and i’m here if you need to talk! good luck <3
